char.peaches.note: Feminine (sie). Name kept; peach jokes use "Pfirsich" only where the joke needs it.

char.minty.note: Masculine (er). Name kept; the flavour is "Minze/minzig".

char.postmaster-bill.note: "Postmeister" = the friendly, old-fashioned title of a post office head. The bill/beak pun does not exist in German.

char.courier.note: One role noun for every bird (generic masculine, used as a title: "Kurier Pip"). Shared story lines never use it about the speaker, so no gender shows. In UI sentences about Peaches/Orbit "Kurierin" is fine.

char.narrator.note: Never shown. Addresses the player with "du".

boss.baron-bat.note: "Baron" + "Fledermaus" (bat); also nods to Strauss's operetta "Die Fledermaus". Short form "der Baron", address "Herr Baron"/"Baron". Addresses the courier with "Sie".

boss.spitter-king.note: "Spuck-" (spit) as in Spuckkäfer. No article on the card; "der Spuckkönig" in sentences; Bill says "König", the birds "Majestät".

boss.dusk-empress.note: "Dämmer-" (dusk) as in Dämmerfalter. Short "die Kaiserin", address "Kaiserin". Addresses the courier with "du".

boss.pirate-captain.note: Short form and self-reference "der Käpt’n"; address "Käpt’n". Speaks pirate-ish ("Ahoi", "Arr", "Donnerwetter", "Landratte" type insults).

boss.ember-dragon.note: "Glut" = embers (old fire that still bites). Short "der Drache", address "Drache".

guardian.neferhoo.note: Name kept. Addresses the courier with "Sie".

guardian.king-coo.note: "gurren" = the German verb for a pigeon cooing; the King Kong echo is lost. Card shout "COO!" -> "GURR!".

guardian.searchlight-gargoyle.note: "Wasserspeier" is the German word for a gargoyle. Card split: "DER SCHEINWERFER-" / "WASSERSPEIER". Short "der Wasserspeier" (also his third-person "Der Wasserspeier nimmt an."). UI short form "Wasserspeier" where the full name does not fit (name 20, bar 16, map plaque); the name card reads "SCHEINWERFER-" / "WASSERSPEIER" on two lines; full form in the defeat banner and the store.

npc.sloth-stargazer.note: "Sterngucker" = playful word for a stargazer. Neuter (das Faultier).

npc.drum-captain.note: Band-leader word, distinct from the Pirate "Käpt’n".

npc.stage-manager.note: Kid-readable; the technical "Inspizient" is unknown to children.

npc.night-cabbies.note: Same people as the cargo's "night-shift cabbies".

npc.kite-flyers.note: "Drachen" is the German word for a kite (as well as dragon); standard usage.

npc.sphinx.note: Standard German "die Sphinx" (grammatically feminine). Peaches calls it "Herr Sphinx" as a cute joke; the note signs "die Sphinx".

title.terror-of-the-high-tide.note: "Flut" = the tide hazard; short for the ribbon.

title.keeper-of-lost-letters.note: Plural club job; echoes the card epithet.

title.royal-courier.note: Same "Kurier" as the courier (Pip's joke works).

title.commissioner-of-the-curb.note: "Kantstein" = curb (where pigeons peck); K-K alliteration, pompous.

title.commissioner.note: Kids know "Kommissar" as the police boss from TV; the pompous third person "Der Kommissar nimmt an." works.

region.open-sea.note: German idiom for the open sea.

place.edge-of-the-map.note: Address form "Rand der Karte"; in speech "am Rand der Karte".

place.sugarloaf-mountain.note: "der Zuckerhut": the German name also means sugar loaf, so Pip's sugar joke survives.

chapter.lamplight-line.note: L-L alliteration, keeps the lamp image.

level.1-7.note: A bat's roost is a "Quartier" in German.

level.3-1.note: Nod to "wie die Motten das Licht".

level.4-5.note: Exact nautical term for spring tide.

level.starter-stair-squats.note: UI (2026-10-07): was "Treppen-Kniebeugen" (18) — over the 16-char starter-name budget. Not spoken.

enemy.purple-bat.note: "lila Fledermaus" where the kind is named.

attack.screech.note: Same root as Bill's "Der kreischt nur".

attack.seed.note: Spat like cherry pits ("Kirschkernspucken"); "Käfer spucken Kerne. Schieß die Kerne ab."

attack.puff.note: Pigeons really "plustern sich auf". POP!/POOF! -> PLOPP!/PUFF!

attack.lamp.note: His chest lamp (the city lamps are "Laternen").

attack.mail-call.note: What a German postman calls out; his attack tag.

pickup.bat-swarm.note: UI duel prize banner (budget 16): "Fledermäuse" ("Fledermäuse auf S2!").

weapon.shoot.note: Button; verb "schießen" in hints ("Schieß die Kerne ab").

ui.sky-club-post.note: Also the doorstep greeting "Himmelsclub-Post!" (like a postman calling "Post!").

ui.stop.note: "Nächster Halt: Paris" (train-announcement style); "Station" also fine in UI.

ui.sky-reclaimed.note: UI (2026-10-07): the victory card uses "HIMMEL BEFREIT" (budget 18; "HIMMEL ZURÜCKEROBERT" is 20). Not spoken.

ui.bonk.note: German cartoon bump; same sound as the Empress's "Klonk. Klonk." and Pip's knockout.

ui.to-be-continued.note: Exact caption the scene player must detect.

ui.play-games.note: Google's German product name is "Google Play Spiele".

ui.home-greeting.target: Hi, ich bin $name! Bereit zum Fliegen?
ui.home-greeting.note: "bereit" is predicative, so it works for all four birds.

achievement.on-the-dot.note: German precision idiom; also literal (the aiming mark).

achievement.flock-together.note: UI (2026-10-07): was "Gemeinsam im Schwarm" (20) — over the 18-char stamp budget; "Bunter Schwarm" (a colourful flock = different birds) is used in the passport and the Play achievement names. Not spoken in any voice clip.

achievement.bright-lights.note: German title of Chaplin's "City Lights": the big-city echo.

story.warm-letter.note: "warm" carries both meanings in German too (warm/herzlich).

story.pigeonholes.note: Pun rebuilt: "Bei uns geht’s zu wie im Taubenschlag, nur ohne Taube." ("wie im Taubenschlag" = constant coming and going, as in a busy post office.)

story.letter-phrases.note: German letter opener and THE German postcard cliché; flight: „Gute Besserung“, „Liebe Grüße“.

story.lamps.note: Street lamps; clear word, no homophone.

story.first-letter.en: the first letter ever sent to the Dragon
story.first-letter.target: der allererste Brief an den Drachen

story.dotted-i.en: He dotted his “i” with a tiny bat.
story.dotted-i.target: Seinen i-Punkt hat er als winzige Fledermaus gemalt.

motto.every-letter-lands.note: Reused verbatim; the Dragon: "Kommt wirklich jeder Brief an?"; Minty: "…und meiner kommt SCHNELL an!"

address.rookie.note: German for greenhorn, literally "green beak": a perfect bird word; epicene in use.

address.little-courier.note: Neuter diminutive: fits any bird, posh condescension.

address.darling.note: Neuter: fits any bird (Gargoyle, Baron, Peaches).

address.postie.note: "carrier pigeon": feminine noun used for any bird; a gruff jibe at a courier bird.

address.sprat.note: The same tiny fish; feminine noun, fits any bird.

address.little-one.note: Neuter; the Empress also says "kleines Wanderherz", "kleiner Nachtvogel".

address.peaches-pet-names.note: Varied set used: Zuckerschnecke, Schätzchen, Honigbärchen, Mäuschen, Zuckerstück, Knuddelkäfer, Butterblümchen, Schnuckelchen, Herzchen, Federchen, Knödelchen…

address.minions.en: Cousins! / my lovelies / my little scarabs / me hearties
address.minions.target: Vettern! / meine Lieblinge / meine kleinen Skarabäen / Mannschaft!

phrase.baron-bat-line.en: This route is my roost now, little courier!
phrase.baron-bat-line.target: Diese Route ist jetzt mein Schlafplatz, Postvögelchen!

phrase.spitter-king-line.en: Every letter on my road goes in the brew!
phrase.spitter-king-line.target: Jeder Brief auf meiner Straße kommt ins Gebräu!

phrase.dusk-empress-line.en: Hush now. The night mail is sleeping.
phrase.dusk-empress-line.target: Pst, still jetzt. Die Nachtpost schläft.

phrase.pirate-captain-line.en: Arr! Every mailbag on these waves be mine!
phrase.pirate-captain-line.target: Arr! Jeder Postsack auf diesen Wellen gehört mir!

phrase.ember-dragon-line.en: The sky is mine. Your letters are kindling.
phrase.ember-dragon-line.target: Der Himmel gehört mir. Deine Briefe sind Zunder.

phrase.neferhoo-line.en: Return to sender! This route has a courier.
phrase.neferhoo-line.target: Zurück an den Absender! Diese Route hat schon einen Kurier.

phrase.king-coo-line.en: Nobody flies till the bread cart is found!
phrase.king-coo-line.target: Keiner fliegt, bis der Brotwagen gefunden ist!

phrase.searchlight-gargoyle-line.en: Hold still! Nobody ever stays in the light.
phrase.searchlight-gargoyle-line.target: Halt doch still! Nie bleibt jemand im Licht.

phrase.return-to-sender.note: Official German postal formula; props: "ZURÜCK AN" / "DEN ABSENDER".

phrase.peaches-tagline.en: Rosy cheeks, curly crest, all heart.
phrase.peaches-tagline.target: Rosa Bäckchen, Lockenschopf, ganz viel Herz.

phrase.minty-tagline.en: Tiny hummer. Fresh sprig. Full speed.

phrase.orbit-tagline.en: A dreamy owl who flies by starlight.
phrase.orbit-tagline.target: Eine verträumte Eule, die im Sternenlicht fliegt.
phrase.orbit-tagline.note: Bill: "Flieg im Sternenlicht, Grünschnabel." UI bird card (budget 48): "Verträumte Eule, die im Sternenlicht fliegt." (article dropped).

phrase.all-screech.note: "Bellende Hunde beißen nicht" spirit, kept short.

phrase.no-flame-seal.en: No flame seal on this guardian.

phrase.at-your-disservice.note: The polite formula, then the twist.

phrase.mind-the-gap.note: Echoes the German platform announcement "Vorsicht an der Bahnsteigkante".

phrase.sticks-and-stones.target: Worte tun nicht weh – aber ich hab Steine dabei!
phrase.sticks-and-stones.note: No German proverb with the same shape; keep the stones joke.

phrase.nobody-looks-up.note: Payoff: "Jeder Kurier wird nach oben schauen!"

phrase.welcome-to-the-club.note: The German idiom exists word for word.

ui.omen-spitter.note: German idiom "something is brewing", literal for him.

story.letter.note: Alphabet sense only in "i-Punkt" and "die Wörter vom Papier kochen".

story.mail-and-post.note: German has one word for both.

story.delivery.note: zustellen / zugestellt; the doorstep "liefern" is fine in speech.

ui.try-again-load.note: Retry after a failed load; "Nochmal" is the level Retry key.

ui.player-short.note: Spieler 1/2; tiny tags and key hints.

ui.greetings-from.note: "Grüße aus" would need the region in the dative.
